name: Carabayo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Carabayo (cara1245) is not in the catalog and cannot be: it is an uncontacted group whose entire linguistic record is ~55 word tokens written down by Capuchin missionaries in 1969. Both Glottolog 'prosody' items in this search of works with stress in the title (Alonso 1984, 1986, 'El Prosodion de Juan Gil de Zamora') are about a 13th-century Latin grammar treatise; the Glottolog reference pages show language code 'Carabayo [cby] (computerized assignment from \"gil\")', i.e. an automatic mis-tag on the word 'Gil' — irrelevant, priority none. The one real analysis, Seifart & Echeverri 2014 (PLoS ONE, open access, downloaded and read, says on p. 2 that acute accents appear on only four wordlist items, are not systematically marked, and are disregarded; it makes no claim about stress placement. The primary 1969 mission-bulletin sources (Juan Berchmans de Felanix 1969; Vidal y Pinell 1970) are print-only and low priority since the 2014 paper reproduces the whole corpus in its Table 1. classification: no stress statement exists for this language; keep it out of the catalog and drop the two mis-tagged Benjamins entries from its bibliography.

new_statements.quote: An acute accent appears in only four items (7, 9 = 18, 10, and 29 = 30). This suggests that whatever it may represent, it was not systematically marked. Therefore we disregard it for establishing hypothetical phoneme inventory.
new_statements.citation: Seifart, Frank & Echeverri, Juan Alvaro (2014). Evidence for the identification of Carabayo, the language of an uncontacted people of the Colombian Amazon, as belonging to the Tikuna-Yurí linguistic family. PLoS ONE 9(4): e94814. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0094814
new_statements.locator: p. 2, Materials and Methods, paragraph on transliteration of Juan Berchmans de Felanix's 1969 list (text file line 122-126); accent-marked items in Table 1, p. 3 (items 7, 9, 10, 18, 29, 30)
new_statements.reading: This is the only first-hand statement bearing on accent in Carabayo that exists in print, and it is a negative one: the whole attested corpus is ~55 word tokens transcribed in 1969 by a Catalan Capuchin missionary in Spanish orthography, acute accents appear on four items only (all, as it happens, on a final syllable: nauué, agó/pin-gó, amá, ané), and the only linguists to analyse the data treat the marking as unsystematic and set it aside. No word-stress placement can be coded for Carabayo from any source; the language should stay out of the catalog (or be recorded as 'no data'). The two Glottolog 'prosody' titles attached to cara1245 are a computerized mis-tag from the word 'Gil' (Juan Gil de Zamora's medieval Latin Prosodion) and should be dropped from the per-language bibliography.

sources.note: The only extant Carabayo data are ~55 word tokens (48 types) written down in 1969 by Capuchin missionaries (Juan Berchmans de Felanix 1969, Amanecer Amazónico XVI:5, 16-17; Venanci d'Arenys de Mar 1969) using Spanish orthography. The authors report that an acute accent appears on only four items of the list (7 ʔa-nauué 'give me, show me'; 9=18 agó / pin-gó 'bring'; 10 amá 'come'; 29=30 ané..), judge the marking unsystematic, and disregard it. sources.citation: Goulard, Jean-Pierre & María Emilia Montes Rodríguez. 2013. Los yurí/juri-tikuna en el complejo socio-lingüístico del Noroeste Amazónico. LIAMES 13: 7-65. doi:10.20396/liames.v0i13.1531
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology/prosody discussion (section 3, incl. 'h) Otras prosodias, tonos bajos..', pp. 20-22) concerns 19th-c. Yurí vs modern Tikuna tones, not Carabayo. On Carabayo, p. 26: the 1969 'caraballo' speech is 'muy mal ejemplificada en un pobre material y aún más pobre transcripción (Berchmans, 1969)'. Anexo 2 (pp. 59-61) reprints Berchmans's 32-item list with its original diacritics (amá, agó, xàma, añé, nya nauué, pinê) and his remark 'Vocalizan muy bien y a diferencia de los Ticunas, tienen pocas vocales neutras. El lenguaje es sonoro y agradable'. No statement about Carabayo stress.

sources.citation: Franco García, Roberto. 2012. Cariba malo: episodios de resistencia de un pueblo indígena aislado del Amazonas. Leticia: Universidad Nacional de Colombia, Sede Amazonia. 204 pp. ISBN 9789587611618.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnohistory of the Yurí/Carabayo. pp. 4-5 summarise Vidal y Pinell's lexical comparison (23% / 21% match with Wallace's Yurí); pp. 123-124 quote Echeverri 2010 (unpublished ACT report) comparing the 'sistemas fonológicos' of caraballo, yurí and passé, segmental only (liquids). Nothing on accent, stress or tone; the 1969 wordlist is not reproduced.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Carabayo language' (en) and 'Idioma carabayo' (es); Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and archive.org searches for 'Carabayo'
sources.note: Both Wikipedia pages give segmental inventories copied from Seifart & Echeverri 2014 and say nothing about stress, accent or tone; the es page lists Echeverri 2010 (ACT report) and Franco 2012 as further literature. Crossref bibliographic search returns only the 2014 PLoS ONE paper for 'Carabayo'; archive.org holds only the PMC copy and Wikipedia snapshots. Ethnologue and endangeredlanguages.com pages were not accessible (not reachable by automated download).

sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Primary source of the entire Carabayo corpus; a mission newspaper, no online copy located. Its content is known only through the reprints in Goulard & Montes 2013 Anexo 2 and Seifart & Echeverri 2014 Table 1: Spanish-orthography items with acute accents on a handful of forms and Berchmans's note that the circumflex marks 'ê neutra francesa'. No stress statement reported by either reprint.
